definitions.explanation: A trick performed by a magician using sleight of hand or props. Literally means 'hand skill' or 'hand technique'.

examples.japanese: ⟦{子供|こども}→子供：00554_kodomo⟧⟦たち→達：01551_tachi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{前|まえ}→前：02255_mae⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{手品|てじな}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{見|み}せた→見せる：01988_miseru⟧。
examples.english: I showed magic tricks in front of the children.

examples.japanese: ⟦トランプ→トランプ：03864_toranpu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{手品|てじな}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{教|おし}えて→教える：00526_oshieru⟧⟦くれませんか→くれる：00724_kureru⟧。
examples.english: Could you teach me a card trick?

examples.japanese: {手品|てじな}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦タネ→種：02157_tane⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦わかりましたか→分かる：00463_wakaru⟧。
examples.english: Did you figure out the trick behind the magic?
examples.notes: タネ = secret, trick (behind a magic trick)

examples.japanese: ⟦{忘年会|ぼうねんかい}→忘年会：15800_bounenkai⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{手品|てじな}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{披露|ひろう}→披露：09683_hirou⟧⟦して→する：00392_suru⟧、⟦みんな→みんな：02972_minna⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{驚|おどろ}かせた→驚く：01255_odoroku⟧。
examples.english: I performed magic tricks at the year-end party and surprised everyone.

notes:
USAGE: {手品|てじな} refers to close-up magic or sleight of hand tricks. It's the everyday word for magic tricks, while ⟦マジック→マジック：11392_majikku⟧ is also commonly used as a loanword.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {手品|てじな}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ (to do a magic trick)
- {手品|てじな}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{見|み}せる→見せる：01988_miseru⟧ (to show a magic trick)
- {手品|てじな}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{披露|ひろう}→披露：09683_hirou⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ (to perform magic - formal)
- ⟦{手品師|てじなし}→手品師：noentry⟧ (magician)

RELATED WORDS:
- ⟦マジック→マジック：11392_majikku⟧ (magic - loanword, more general)
- ⟦{魔法|まほう}→魔法：14640_mahou⟧ (magic - supernatural, not tricks)
- ⟦{奇術|きじゅつ}→奇術：23680_kijutsu⟧ (magic arts - more formal)
- ⟦{手品師|てじなし}→手品師：noentry⟧/マジシャン (magician)

Note: {手品|てじな} implies skill and technique rather than supernatural power, unlike ⟦{魔法|まほう}→魔法：14640_mahou⟧.
